name: Pale Peach
lede: Pale Peach is a light, creamy pink-orange, the color of a peach's skin faded almost to cream.

sections.title: Moonlight, in an old list
sections.body:
The name is a lightened [[peach]], the fruit color [3]. It is listed in the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 and in Ridgway's 1912 color book [3].

St Clair's glossary of color words uses it to define another name: moonlight is a very pale peach [1]. It is a fact about how the word is defined, not a claim about real moonlight [1]. Nearby names include [[apricot]] and [[cream]] [3].

The swatch on this page is #FFE5AD, the screen value we hold for it, which is an approximation and not a measured pigment [3]. Like any pale color it sits between its hue and [[white]], and because the name is a description and not a tradition, other lists may place it a little differently [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Pale Peach is common among pale colors in our archive: 457 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.92 percent, as photographed [2]. It is commoner than 71 percent of the named colors, and peaks in the 1800s, found in 102 of the 8,345 paintings from that century, about 1.3 times the museums' baseline rate [2].
